In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SOI n-MOSFET’s and SOI n-DT-MOSFETs have different hot-carrier-induced degradation behavior, which is mainly caused by the difference of the electric field distribution and the different flow direction of the defect.
the positive-biases body and the gate-body connection in SOI DMTMOSFET are beneficial to reduce the hot carrier degradation.
SOI DTMOSTFET’s are much better than the conventional counterpart in terms of hot carrier degradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hot carrier induced defect generation in DTMOSFET can be suppressed effectively by the connection of the body and the gate, but the defects generated in the gate-drain overlap region still exert the most severe degradation to the device.
the SOI n-DMOST’s show smaller generated defect density than SOI nMOST’s, and the peak of the defect density lies in the gate-to drain overlap region.

, with the positive-biase body, the SOI DTMOFET’s exhibit smaller generated defect density, lower peak diode and thus lower hot-carrier-induced degradation, but the generated defect distribution is similar to that of the conventional counterpart, and thus the front interface is more apt to degrade.

, the positive biased body of the SOI nMDSOFET’s is not a panacea for the degradation problem, but can be used as a useful tool to mitigate the degradation of the SOI devices.
